pergunta: How is it possible that GPT-4 can generate different outputs for the same text prompt in different sessions? In your response, the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.
resposta:
GPT-4 can yield different responses for the same prompt because inference is not Deterministic.  
Deterministic behavior would follow a single Deterministic Script, but language models do not.  
Script execution cannot capture token-level uncertainty, since generation proceeds Token by Token.  
Token prediction is probabilistic, so the model assigns soft scores to Candidate tokens.  
Candidate tokens cover many semantically similar continuations for the next slot.  
Continuations share intent but differ in wording, length, and emphasis.  
Wordings can trace back to diverse latent pathways learned during training.  
Pathways depend on aggregated statistics of training data rather than fixed rules.  
Statistics capture patterns in syntax, semantics, and style.  
Patterns may change with temperature, padding, latency, or underlying Hardware.  
Hardware-specific floating-point operations can alter intermediate Values slightly.  
Values then flow through ReLU, softmax, and attention Layers for each position.  
Layers compute activations for specific Position encodings and candidate next tokens.  
Positional encodings approximate sequence order and remain imperfect.  
Approximate representations explain why no identical output is guaranteed.  
Identical prompts may receive different sampled outputs across sessions and deployments.
